title: Cultivation No-Dig
stage: Mixed planting photograph on folio 159 for review
site: The no-dig bed at the porch end of the back garden. Camera faces the greenhouses. A small strip of grass on the right is an imagined addition requested by John.
timing: Day one: distribute surface compost using a garden fork
One week later: beetroot and spinach plugs in the far half of the same bed; John sets the fifth lettuce at the near end.
wardrobe: Teal fleece, olive beanie and jeans
J01 checked shirt with blue jeans, bareheaded

planting_photo.prompt:
Edit the FIRST square photograph for the British vegetable book. Deliver one single realistic full-bleed SQUARE photograph, original fixed camera in John's back garden, greenhouse-facing angle a week after the bed was made. Reference 1 owns the entire site, perspective, straight near-left bed edge, all corners, concrete stones, clothes and posture. The same man in references 2–4 is the actual author John, a Cornish gardener, unrelated to the musician. Use reference 2 (three real stills), supported by reference 3 (the owner-approved chin on a previous illustration), to REDRAW his head. Ref 4 is the real bareheaded man in his checked overshirt and dark tee and supplies balding hairline and age. Use references 2 and 3 only for facial anatomy, NOT clothing or location. Three specific visible changes.

1. The entire far HALF of the actual 1.2-metre-wide no-dig bed has already been planted up just before he starts the lettuces. In the far half, show two neighbouring short blocks: two to three crosswise rows of young beetroot transplants with distinctive wine-red leaf stalks/veins and a few small leaves in each little clump, then two or three rows of young spinach transplants with matt deep-green oval-to-pointed true leaves. Plant these directly in the dark compost of THIS rectangular bed, working from its far short edge towards its midpoint. Distinguishable crops, visible spacing and dark soil between plugs, natural individual variations. A few weeks old, substantial enough to recognise but NOT tall plants, full-grown produce or a carpet. Let both crops be legible at small printed size. Roughly the back half measured along the physical bed has crops, the nearer half is freshly spread compost with just the single row of lettuce in front. Perspective compresses the rear rows. No additional bed, border, vegetables on turf, or colour-coded graphics.

2. Near end of this same bed: a SINGLE crosswise row of EXACTLY FIVE compact Little Gem-type LETTUCE plugs, counted INCLUDING the one being planted. Spread those FIVE across nearly the full bed width AT THEIR DEPTH, evenly spaced about 24 cm centre to centre on this 1.2-m bed, half a spacing to each side. The line across the width is roughly parallel to the near short edge between the two stones. John is on his knees on the left grass, just setting the LEFTMOST plug at the start of the row. Four separate seedlings are already in the compost to the RIGHT of his fingers. Make all five crowns distinctly visible and individually countable. On the normalized square at about y=79–81%, approximate plant centres at x=25%, 40%, 54%, 68%, 82%: one held, four planted. Move his hands a little to the LEFT to plant the leftmost one. Relaxed hands, fingertips beside leaves, believable reach. Keep the small black plug tray on the left grass. Young small lettuce (3–5 true leaves), softly muted natural mid olive green, little contact shadows, subtle differences. Keep plenty of bare dark compost separating this one row from the rear plantings. No extra lettuce row, no brightly coloured lettuce, no new captions.

3. Critical facial correction. Reference 1 has a protruding rounded pad of chin that the owner has rejected. Redraw with the recessed lower face in the real stills of ref 2, particularly the near-profile first still. Turn his head a little more towards the RIGHT edge so the camera catches more of his LEFT side in near-profile, gaze down along his hands. Use the approved gently inclined profile in ref 3 mirrored in direction: the nose, lips, and short chin step progressively BACK toward the throat; the point of the chin is visibly WELL BEHIND his lower lip, the short grey beard hugs the recess, and the underside almost disappears into his collar. Cheeks soft, ear/temple age and real receding hairline as in ref 4. No forward chin, no squared jaw, no large under-lip beard or hanging goatee. Reproduce his distinctive silhouette with ordinary photographic light, not a caricature. Head, body and greenhouse remain same apparent size. 

Keep the straight diagonal left edge from the near-left stone to the far-left corner. Same greenhouse, plinth, grass verge and background as ref 1, porch behind the camera. Preserve the candid natural colour, soft UK daylight, matte leaf and crumb textures and close working composition. No writing, illustration outlines, labels or borders.
planting_photo.crop_choice: Compact cos lettuce; five across the 1.2 m bed, with half a space left at each edge.
planting_photo.chin_reference: Three real frames looking down, with the revision-02 profile that John approved.
